findings.message: The comment in resolveSummariser still describes the summariser factory as the 'summariser-stays-local decoupling'. After this Story the summariser follows the cheap tier, which defaults to the Claude CLI pinned to haiku. The line-80 doc comment was updated but this one was missed, so the file now contradicts itself about where the summariser runs.
findings.expectationRef: dataModelChanges['Docs and comments naming the defaults']: the comments in src/analyze/context/role-router.ts that say peripheral roles go to local and the summariser stays local are brought in line with the summariser following the cheap tier

findings.message: SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK hard-codes the cheap model for each CLI ('haiku' for cli-claude, 'gpt-6-luna' for cli-codex). The same ids are already the built-in cheap tier: DEFAULT_TIERS.cheap.model in src/config/analyze.ts, which resolveTiers reads; config-catalog's models.tiers.cheap.model default; and the installer's codex cheap tier. If the default cheap model changes in one place and not here, a CLI summariser handed an Ollama-shaped id would quietly fall back to a stale model. Deriving the claude entry from DEFAULT_TIERS.cheap.model, or keeping one per-CLI cheap-model map that both places use, would remove the drift. It is not wrong today because all copies agree.
